title: EMS Director
statement:
**EMS Director's Weekly Report — Cycle 117 (on the record)**

Two ambulance runs this Cycle: one in Piedmont Ave, one in Grand Lake, both minor injury, both landing with modest negative sentiment on the block. Small numbers — but I still want my crews to log what they saw on those two blocks. "What the block saw" is blank in my copy, and blanks in this job are how patterns hide.

Hospital intakes citywide came to 34, all illness, all discharged by end of Cycle — zero in care carried over, zero beds occupied at close. Injury, heat, mental-health-crisis, substance-treatment, unclassified: all zero. For a city this size, 34 illness intakes with a full turnover is a quiet week, and I'll say so plainly rather than dress it up.

By neighborhood, illness intakes ran 1–3 apiece, with Chinatown highest at 3 (6 in care during the Cycle, all released). Downtown, Jack London and Brooklyn had 1 each. KONO, Lake Merritt, Uptown, Baylight District and my own neighborhood recorded zero intakes. And here is what I want on the record: our "residents sick" count is a different picture entirely. Chinatown 133, East Oakland 113, Ivy Hill 109, Fruitvale 108, San Antonio 104 — those are sick residents who did not come through our intake doors. Uptown, Lake Merritt, KONO and Baylight sit in the teens. Intakes of 34 against hundreds sick citywide means most people are riding it out at home. That is fine this week. It will not be fine if it holds and then turns.

The tracked ledger shows no admissions in 117; the only residents listed are past recoveries — Yu Zen and Maurice Franklin of Rockridge, Deacon Seymour of Lake Merritt — all discharged and recovered. Three residents are still waiting on an assigned cause — Marcus Osei in Chinatown, Elliott Crane in Uptown, Ariana Lee in Piedmont Ave on a serious cancer course — and I want those causes closed out in the record, not left hanging.

No open health arcs, no health events on the city's event ledger, and the domain tracker shows health at zero events this Cycle — though the tracker's total line reads 10, which I read as volume elsewhere in the city, not in my domain.

What I'm telling the Mayor and the council: a quiet intake week is the week to fill in the blanks — the two ambulance narratives and those three pending causes — and to get a real read on the sick-at-home numbers while they're still small. I'd rather answer for a quiet week I prepared in than a loud one I didn't.

— Priya Narang, EMS Director, Uptown
